November in images: collaborative portraiture, new London exhibitions, and fashion campaigns built through distinct creative voices.

London / Fashion / Portraiture

Davide Studios

Monthly Newsletter — November Issue

November’s images return to the people who make them. A new studio portrait series draws on Pre-Raphaelite detail, while London exhibitions consider identity, self-portraiture and the making of worlds. In fashion, an intimate festive tableau, a city in motion and a country-house gathering offer three ways to build a story through setting and collaboration.
 

01 — Art

Portraiture, design and the construction of a visual world in London.

Installation view, The Nue Black Aesthetic. Photograph: Christian Cassiel / Design Museum.

Design Museum / 224–238 Kensington High Street, London W8 6AG / 6 November 2026 – 8 August 2027

The Nue Black Aesthetic

Guest-curated by Charlene Prempeh, The Nue Black Aesthetic brings together more than 100 objects across fashion, furniture, architecture, product design and sculpture. The exhibition resists a single definition of Black design, allowing distinct practices and diasporic histories to sit alongside one another. Its installations make a case for seeing identity as a source of many visual languages, rather than one fixed style.

Why it matters visually: The show foregrounds the individual point of view behind each object, then lets those voices meet in one shared space.

View exhibition

The Photographers’ Gallery, Print Sales Gallery / 16–18 Ramillies Street, London W1F 7LW / 26 November 2026 – 24 January 2027

Juno Calypso: Empty Pleasures

Juno Calypso’s staged self-portraits return alongside new collage and found imagery. Pastel interiors, mirrored figures and fragments from photographs of the 1970s and 1980s form an uneasy theatre of beauty and aspiration. Her solitary performances make the work feel both intimate and constructed, asking how much of a portrait belongs to the person in it and how much to the image they are expected to perform.

Why it matters visually: Calypso uses styling, repetition and the set itself to expose the pressure behind a seemingly perfect image.

View exhibition

Design Museum / 224–238 Kensington High Street, London W8 6AG / 2 October 2026 – 4 April 2027

Es Devlin: Other Worlds

The Design Museum traces three decades of Es Devlin’s work across sculpture, stage design, film, language and light. A replica of her studio places books, objects and maquettes beside early drawings and collages; a circular desk gathers projects from theatre, concerts and public installations. The exhibition makes visible the patient thinking behind large-scale spectacle, from an initial mark on paper to a space experienced by many people.

Why it matters visually: The studio archive shows how image-making grows through sketches, materials, spatial decisions and collaboration.

View exhibition
 

02 — Fashion

Three campaigns in which people, place and styling build the narrative together.

Miu Miu / Holiday 2026 campaign

An Uptown Fairytale

Tina Barney photographs Miu Miu’s holiday cast inside a townhouse dressed with fir branches, polished wood and winter light. The scenes have the formality of a family portrait, loosened by plush animals and unexpected pairings of tailoring, sequins and outerwear. Barney’s eye for domestic theatre gives each person room to occupy the frame, while styling and setting turn a seasonal gathering into a layered picture of character.

Source visual: Official Miu Miu Holiday 2026 campaign image. Photograph: Tina Barney.

View official source

LOEWE / Spring Summer 2027 precollection, available from 12 November 2026

Madrid, in Motion

LOEWE’s precollection follows Diego Calva, Victoria Luengo, Kristine Frøseth and Jiang Qiming through Madrid’s markets, modernist buildings and tiled bars. Talia Chetrit and Julian Klincewicz photograph bold colour and hybrid materials against the city’s changing surfaces. The campaign’s value lies in the relationship between wardrobe and location: a garment shifts character as a person moves through different rooms, streets and moments of the day.

Source visual: Official LOEWE Spring Summer 2027 precollection campaign image. Photography: Talia Chetrit and Julian Klincewicz.

View official source

Burberry / Festive 2026 campaign, launched 3 November

Wrapped in Burberry

For its 170th year, Burberry gathers a cast at Longleat House for a playful country-house celebration directed by Harmony Korine. Fiona Shaw and Pierce Brosnan welcome guests from film, fashion and sport, making the campaign feel populated rather than posed in isolation. Checks, outerwear and the rooms themselves create a shared visual language. Its energy comes from the way distinct personalities inhabit one setting, each adding a note to the larger picture.

Source visual: Official Burberry Festive 2026 campaign image. Film direction: Harmony Korine.

View official source
 

03 — On the Field

A portrait made through shared imagination.

Studio Notes: Of Earth and Ether

This month’s portrait series takes its cue from Pre-Raphaelite portraiture: unbound hair, flowers, layered fabric and a gaze that holds the frame. We followed those details into a contemporary studio image, looking for a balance between quiet theatricality and the presence of the person in front of the camera.

Photograph: Davide Studios / Of Earth and Ether

The first portrait lets the hair and small flowers fill the space around Julianna. Styling, texture and pose were developed together, with every adjustment changing the shape of the picture. An editorial set becomes stronger when a trusted team can respond to what is happening in front of them, rather than simply execute a fixed plan.

Photograph: Davide Studios / Of Earth and Ether

The closer frame brings the exchange into focus. Each person’s opinion matters: a suggestion about a sleeve, a shift in the hair, or a different way to hold the light can open a better image. Speaking up gives the whole team a chance to build on an idea, and gives the subject room to shape it too.

Photograph: Davide Studios / Of Earth and Ether

In the final frame, the flowers travel through the hair against a darker ground. What began as a reference to painting became something made by this particular group of people. Strong editorial photographs carry the decisions of everyone who helped make them.
